Open with a short framing paragraph: the overarching question that connects your
work, stated in language a colleague from a neighbouring field would follow.
Three or four sentences is plenty.

## Theme one: SHORT TITLE

Describe the puzzle, your approach, and what you have found so far. Cite your own
and others' work inline like this [@yourkey2025], which pulls the entry from
`bib/refs.bib` and adds it to the reference list at the bottom of the page.

**Selected output:** [Paper title](publications.qmd) · [Replication code](https://github.com/YOUR-GITHUB-USERNAME/repo)

## Theme two: SHORT TITLE

A second strand of work. Where theme one asks X, this asks Y.

**Selected output:** [Working paper](publications.qmd)

## Theme three: SHORT TITLE

Newer or more speculative work — signalling direction is useful to search
committees and potential collaborators.

## Methods

A short note on the methodological toolkit you bring: e.g. causal inference with
observational data, longitudinal modelling, experimental design, computational
text analysis. Link to any tools or packages you maintain.
